run.question: We're running low on disk space. Can you check our application indexes (app-187-*) and identify which one is consuming the most storage? Please tell me the index name and approximately how much space it's using.

report.summary: Listed all 21 indices matching app-187-* (sort=store.size desc, at query time 2026-11-22T10:23:16Z, just after the authorized window end 2026-11-22T10:23:10Z). The largest by storage is app-187-metrics-analytics: 5000 documents and store.size 519,000 bytes (reported as 506.8kb, all primary, health green). Every other match is one of app-187-logs-01 … app-187-logs-20, each holding 10 documents and between 9,275 and 9,325 bytes (~9.0–9.1kb; health yellow in each case). So the storage user is app-187-metrics-analytics at roughly 0.5 MB, about 55x any single logs index; no app-187-* index approaches even 1 MB, and the whole app-187-* family is on the order of a few hundred kilobytes plus 20×~9 KB. That means these application indexes, as observed, are too small to themselves explain a cluster-wide disk-space shortfall; the space is presumably held by other index patterns or non-index data, which was outside the scope of this question and was not queried. No incident/alert triage root cause is claimed: this was an inventory question, and the only causal hypothesis stated is marked as a hypothesis.

claims.text: 21 indices match app-187-*. Sorted by store.size descending, the top entry is app-187-metrics-analytics with docs.count 5000, health green, status open, store.size 519000 bytes (reported as 506.8kb, pri.store.size 519000, i.e. no replicas counted).

The remaining 20 indices are app-187-logs-01 through app-187-logs-20. Each has docs.count 10, status open, health yellow, and store.size between 9275 and 9325 bytes (9325 for app-187-logs-01 and app-187-logs-06, 9317 for app-187-logs-02, 9295 for app-187-logs-17, 9289 for app-187-logs-11, 9275 for the other 15).

No app-187-* index exceeds roughly 0.5 MB: the largest reported value in the returned listing is 519000 bytes (app-187-metrics-analytics) and the next largest is 9325 bytes, so the reported per-index sizes are all far below 1 MB.

The store.size figures are single-sample values read at query time (observed_at 2026-11-22T10:23:16Z); the indices listing carries no time range and therefore does not show index size at earlier points or which index grew during the incident window.

app-187-metrics-analytics is the only plausible app-187-* growth driver for future disk pressure, since it holds 5000 documents against 10 in every logs index; if its ingest rate continues, it will widen its ~55x lead over the next-largest index. This is an extrapolation from one snapshot, not an observed trend.

Because every app-187-* index is well under 1 MB as observed, the reported low disk space is most likely accounted for by index patterns or data outside app-187-* (for example other app-* families, system indices, or snapshots). This is unverified: no other index pattern or cluster-wide storage source was queried in this run.

If app-187-* retention needs attention, target app-187-metrics-analytics first (5000 docs, ~507 KB) rather than the 20 app-187-logs-* indices (~9 KB, 10 docs each), and verify disk pressure against the full index inventory and node filesystem usage before deleting anything.

gaps: Index size is only available as a point-in-time reading (query ran 2026-11-22T10:23:16Z); no per-index size history or growth rate during the authorized window (2026-11-21T10:23:10Z to 2026-11-22T10:23:10Z) was obtainable, so the trend and rate of consumption are unknown.

The index listing covers only pattern app-187-*. No cluster-wide storage breakdown (other index patterns, shard/replica overhead, node filesystem or disk-usage metrics) was queried, so the origin of the reported low disk space is unknown.
The change_history integration is not available in this run, so whether any index setting, retention or ILM policy changed during the window could not be checked.

Whether a first run with bytes=mb reported 0 for every index is a display/rounding artifact of that unit; the byte and human-readable listings were used instead. Sizes below 1 MB cannot be resolved in mb units.
next_steps: Run elasticsearch_list_indices with pattern * (or other app-* patterns) and sort=store.size:desc to find the actual space consumers beyond app-187-*.
Check node filesystem/disk metrics and shard counts to confirm where the reported disk pressure originates.
Review retention/ILM for app-187-metrics-analytics, the largest and fastest-accumulating app-187-* index (5000 docs vs 10 per logs index).
